title: 11-Year-Old Bodhana Makes Chess History
summary: Imagine becoming one of the best chess players in the world before you finish middle school! That is true for Bodhana Sivanandan, an 11-year-old from northwest London, England. On September 26, 2026, she became the youngest person ever to earn the Woman Grandmaster title. The old record was held by Kateryna Lagno, who was 12 in 2002. To earn this high honor, a player must reach a rating of at least 2,300 points and meet special rules in three qualifying tournaments, called norms. Bodhana found chess in 2020, when she was five, after finding a chessboard in a bag of toys and books. At age seven, she won all 24 of her games at the European Schools Championship. At age 10, she beat Grandmaster Peter Wells. In August 2026, she became the youngest-ever British women's chess champion. The next month, at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, she won six games, drew four, and lost one, earning her final norm. She now hopes to earn the Grandmaster title, which is open to players of any gender.
why_it_matters: It shows kids that starting small and practicing can lead to big achievements, even before finishing middle school.
